name: now-playing
title: Now Playing
description: A dark music widget: the cover springs forward on play, the icon morphs and progress runs on the UI thread.

perf.budget: Progress is one UI-thread timing per track; the time labels re-render four times a second while playing. Paused, nothing animates.

a11y.reducedMotion: Play, pause and skipping change state without the cover spring, slide or icon turn.
a11y.screenReader: Title and subtitle read as one line; the progress is adjustable ("1:09 of 3:43", ten-second steps); Previous, Play/Pause and Next are buttons.
a11y.touchTarget: Buttons are 44 pt tall; the progress bar's touch area is 44 pt tall.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { NowPlaying } from '@/components/kinetik/now-playing';

<NowPlaying
  tracks={queue.map((t) => ({
    id: t.id,
    title: t.title,
    subtitle: t.artist,
    cover: { uri: t.artwork },
    duration: t.seconds,
  }))}
  onTrackChange={(t) => player.load(t.id)}
  onPlayingChange={(on) => (on ? player.play() : player.pause())}
/>;
```

## When to use

- A compact player for a queue: a widget, a mini player or a now-playing sheet header.

## When not to use

- As the source of truth for real audio: it keeps its own clock. Wire `onPlayingChange` and `onTrackChange` to your player, and keep the two in step.

## Notes

- Previous restarts the track if more than three seconds have played, as most players do; otherwise it goes back a track.
- Tap the progress bar to seek. Screen readers adjust it in ten-second steps.
- When a track ends, the next one starts. The queue wraps around.
- `clock(seconds)` is exported for the same `1:09` format elsewhere.
- The widget is dark on both themes. `accent` colours the progress and the play button.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add now-playing`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
